title: Sculpture recreates odd optical effects of famed Lycurgus Cup
gist: University of Sheffield scientists Lisa Hollands and Caroline Jackson developed a replicable glass recipe reproducing the Roman Lycurgus Cup's dichroic effect (green in reflected light, red when backlit), caused by gold and silver nanoparticles. The work sits within the UK Molecular Photonic Breadboards project on light-harnessing materials for sustainable technologies, and glass artist Elliott Walker used it for a new sculpture.

insights.claim: The Lycurgus Cup's color shift from green in reflected light to red in transmitted light was explained in 2007 as the effect of gold and silver nanoparticles that alter how electrons vibrate in response to light.
